Description: An IPv4 address that belongs to somebody
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
refactor: split every file over the 150-line gate, and re-enable it

Thirteen files, split by responsibility rather than by size: parsers away
from the plugins that use them, wire framing away from transport setup,
the daemon's subcommands away from the daemon. Tests moved with what they
cover.

The gate lost its exemption list along with the last offender.

resilumd::daemon returns instead of exiting, so the iroh handle is still
dropped on the way out — its teardown sends CONNECTION_CLOSE.

Description: A path under a build host's home directory
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
check: gate comment density and index leaks, and require every tool

cargo-deny exits 0 on its own warnings and a missing linter was skipped
with a note, so both printed findings under a green tick. Renamed imports
are refused through ast-grep, which matches the AST node rather than text.

The leak gate reads the index rather than the working tree: skip-worktree
hides local edits only while that flag survives, and it lives in
.git/index.

sha2 and hmac move to the versions the rest of the tree already resolves
to.

Description: An IPv4 address that belongs to somebody
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
egress: embedded SOCKS5 backend and rename connect: -> ingress:

Adds a SOCKS5 server-side handshake so `service: socks-egress` with no
`target` handles the CONNECT protocol in-process — no external microsocks
or dante daemon on the exit host. Splits IngressConfig into its own module
and renames the yaml key to reflect that the section pairs symmetrically
with egress: (accept local traffic, forward through the mesh).

Description: An IPv4 address that belongs to somebody
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
discovery/covert: attach peers as runtime PipeInterface subprocesses

CovertDiscovered.consume_endpoint now spawns a task that fetches the
peer endpoint over the encrypted rendezvous link, renders the
per-carrier client-command template (dst / server_identity /
mtu placeholders), and attaches a PipeInterface via
Node::spawn_pipe_client. Handles are kept per-peer-pubkey so a
re-announce doesn't re-attach.

Also strips a stray comment from the previous rendezvous responder.

Description: An IPv4 address that belongs to somebody
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
discovery: extend plugin trait with announcer pubkey; add covert plugin skeleton

Trait now passes the announcer's identity pubkey to consume_endpoint —
covert carriers need it to fetch the endpoint over an authenticated link
(TCP-discovery ignores it). Capability-only announces (no endpoint in
app_data) are routed too.

Adds CovertDiscoveryService config + CovertDiscovered plugin skeleton
(produce=None, consume=log). Rendezvous fetch + pipe attach in next
slices. Endpoint pack/parse with proptest roundtrip + garbage-never-
panics guard.

Description: An IPv4 address that belongs to somebody
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
net: local egress address probe; discovery/covert: auto-fill addresses when none configured

Adds crate::net::local_egress_addresses — UDP-connect trick to a
well-known IPv4/IPv6 anchor, kernel picks the source, returned only if
globally-routable (private/loopback/link-local/ULA/documentation dropped).
Portable stdlib; no packets leave the host.

AddressSource is what the covert plugin and its rendezvous responder
consult for the effective address list: explicit config wins, otherwise
fall back to auto-detect at plugin construction. Same Arc shared between
producer and responder so both see the same list.

discovery::build_from_services grows a BuildParams struct rather than
sprouting positional arguments. Extracted to a new build.rs to keep
discovery/mod.rs under the file-size cap.

Description: An IPv4 address that belongs to somebody
Author: resilum-owner
Message:
core: connect side — discover, select, forward and probe egress candidates

Add the connect side that accepts local TCP and forwards each connection
through the fastest eligible egress candidate:

- announce_payload: JSON envelope (version/endpoint/country/capabilities),
 wire-compatible; listen now advertises exit_country
- discover: populate the candidate registry from egress announces
- connect: local listener -> eligible+choose_best (sticky) -> dial (recalling
 the peer key via get_identity) -> byte pump
- probe/monitor: e2e SOCKS5 probe over a fresh link and a latency monitor that
 writes link_rtt/egress_side back to the registry for selection

leviculum exposes no link RTT, so link_rtt is derived from the SOCKS greeting
round-trip rather than a warm link. Covered by unit tests and a two-node
connect->egress->echo round-trip.
